Shaped like this phone\'s screen, black with the code on a white card — on any phone it looks full screen. “Share → As a picture” or “Save to gallery” gives an image exactly in screen pixels. Printing stays on white.
Delete the folder with its codes
All codes in this folder (%1$d) will be deleted for good together with it. They can’t be restored.
The folder is empty — it will be deleted.

• Swipe left from “Favourites” or tap “Create” at the top.
• Type in the capsule at the bottom — the code appears above at once.
• The round button on the right — save; the field clears.
• The icon on the left of the capsule — input mode: by hand, scan someone’s QR, text from a photo, plus Wi‑Fi, contact and site.
• “QR code / Barcode” above the preview — what to create. The choice is remembered.
• Text shared from another app lands in the field by itself.
• “Many codes at once” (the icon on the left of the capsule): a numbered series (PALLET-001…100) or a list — all into a new folder; when printing — “Each code on its own label”.
• The third button next to “QR code / Barcode” — the type of the chosen one: for QR — QR, Data Matrix, Aztec; for barcodes — Auto, EAN-8, UPC, Code 39 and more.
• “Scanner forms”: a “live” QR that fills fields in turn. Fields: text, scan (camera, photo, by hand), choice from a list, number, “from field” (another field’s value + an ending, e.g. P), date by your own pattern. Before scanning switch any field on or off (the cursor skips switched-off ones), the QR changes at once; scan it from the screen.
Camera and text from a photo

• “Scan QR” — point the camera at a code, its copy appears, save it.
• “Text from photo” — take a photo, found words get frames.
• Tap a word — choose or drop it.
• Hold a word and drag — everything up to your finger is chosen.
• The square next to a line — the whole line.
• “Done” — the choice goes into the field, where you can fix it.
• Both modes can take a picture from the gallery. The torch is a button on the camera screen.

• Tap a code — full screen, brightness to the max so it scans easily.
• Swipe left — delete (with “Undo”).
• Long press and release — menu: favourite, name, content (view and fix), print, copy, to a folder, delete.
• Your own name hides the content — handy for passwords.
• The magnifier in the capsule — search by name or content.

• Hold a code and drag — change the order.
• Drop a code onto another code — a new folder with both.
• Drop a code onto a folder — it goes inside.
• Tap a folder — open it; the arrow at the top or “Back” — leave.
• Long press a folder — name, print all codes, ungroup (codes stay) or delete with everything inside.
• In a code’s menu: “To a folder…” and “Take out of the folder”.

• The star in a code’s menu — add to favourites.
• “Favourites” is the first page, codes in a grid.
• Hold and drag — change the order.
• Drop onto the bar at the top — remove from favourites (with “Undo”).

• Top right — “Share” (picture, gallery, text) and the blue “Print”.
• Under the label: the “Add” and “Edit” tabs, and on the right the label size (ready ones, your own, “Phone screen”).
• “Add”: code, text, icon, finger drawing, backdrop (your own picture or a scene with spots for codes — codes sit on a solid pad; move, scale, turn or rub it out with the eraser under “Edit” → “Backdrop”; drawings have an eraser too), template, frame.
• Tap an item — it is chosen and “Edit” opens: size, turn, centre, copy, caption, replace, undo, delete.
• Nothing chosen — “Edit” works on the whole label: grid, undo, delete everything (it asks first).
• “Drawing” — draw with your finger right on the label (thin, thick, eraser), “Done” — and it is an item.
• Drag — move; two fingers — size and turn; double tap — edit the text, caption or icon.
• Drag onto “Delete” at the top — remove.
• Items snap to the edges and centres of the label and of other items, equal gaps are shown as marked segments; nothing overlaps or leaves the label.
• Your layout, codes included, can be saved as a template and opened ready later.

• The gear at the top right — style (Black Glass or Black Sketch) and language.
• “Export” — all codes, folders and templates in one file, e.g. for a new phone.
• “Import” — bring them back from a file; only what is new is added.
• The app works offline: it sends nothing anywhere.
Codes sit on a solid pad, so the picture under them never gets in the scanner’s way. Move, enlarge or turn the backdrop under “Edit” → “Backdrop”.
Backdrop chosen: drag — move, two fingers — zoom in, out and turn. Whatever is past the edge is simply hidden.
Scenes — codes drop into the squares
Eraser: run your finger over the label — the backdrop under it is wiped. “Undo” brings it back.
Draw with your finger right on the label. The drawing never covers codes.
Everything encoded is here (%1$d characters). Fix it and the code changes; the name, folder and favourite stay.
Content this long won’t fit into a QR code
A barcode takes only Latin letters, digits and signs (up to 48), or 13 EAN digits
Your unsaved label is back, just as you left it
The most common: any text, links, Wi‑Fi, any alphabet
Small square — tiny parts and medicine; Latin letters only
Square without a margin — tickets, boarding passes; any text
Picks by itself: EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A for digits with a check digit, otherwise Code 128
Warehouse and logistics: Latin letters, digits, signs (up to 48)
Older scanners and industry: A–Z, 0–9, - . $ / + % space
US and Canada goods: 11 or 12 digits
Boxes and pallets: an even number of digits
Libraries, labs: digits and - $ : / . +, starts and ends with A–D
From a list — each line is a code
First number, how many codes and how many digits in the number (3 — 001, 002…; 0 — no zeros).
Paste or type: each line becomes a separate code
Not valid for this code type: %1$d.
Each code on its own label (%1$d)
With this layout: every label gets its own code. Handy for series and folders.
No app on this phone can do that
A character between fields — set the scanner to replace it with a key (e.g. ↓ down arrow): Zebra — ADF, Honeywell — Data Formatter.
No forms yet. Create the first one — the fields the scanner should fill in turn.
A form is a “live” QR: open it, fit the fields to the task (scan, choice, number; any field can be switched off — the cursor just skips it) and scan the code straight from the screen.
The form will be deleted. Saved codes stay.
When filling in: camera (code), text from a photo or by hand.
Options — one per line (e.g. dock numbers)
Takes the value of a field (pick its number) — add a prefix or ending below.
Today’s date by pattern: dd — day, MM — month, yyyy — year (yy — two digits); spaces and other signs stay as they are.
First skip %1$d field(s) on the scanner with the down arrow, then scan.
Scan, press the arrow on the scanner and tap the code — the next field appears.
